bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Information security, customer data privacy and DPDP compliance — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as the Company's first material risk with negative financial implications. As a digital travel platform it processes significant volumes of customers' personal information; risks include data breaches, cyber threats, unauthorized access, non-compliance with evolving regulatory requirements including the Digital Personal Data Protection framework, third-party security vulnerabilities, operational disruptions, reputational damage, financial penalties, litigation and loss of customer confidence. Mitigated through the ERM framework, Risk Management Committee oversight, information security controls, incident response and breach management, periodic vulnerability assessments and penetration testing, and review of consent management and third-party data processing arrangements.
- Ineffective internal financial controls over financial reporting and the resulting auditor qualification — The auditors identified weaknesses in the operating effectiveness of internal financial controls as at March 31, 2026 on both a standalone and consolidated basis - inadequate documentation evidencing review of control attributes over revenue, receivables, payables, service cost, significant estimates and the financial-statement closing process for the packages business, and design gaps and operating ineffectiveness of ITGC controls in the hotel business, plus an audit-trail (edit log) compliance gap under Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules. Management's remediation principally involves upgrading the primary accounting software from MS Navision to D365 F&O.
- Regulatory scrutiny of IPO proceeds utilisation — An Emphasis of Matter in the auditor's report draws attention to queries received from the National Stock Exchange and SEBI in respect of deposits/advances aggregating INR 3,391.44 million given from IPO proceeds till June 30, 2024. The Company has responded and, based on legal opinions, management considers the classification to be in accordance with the offer document's object clause; the auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of the matter.
- Talent attraction, attrition and human capital development — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: lack of talent with required skills, high attrition and low human capital development may cause business disruptions, harm reputation and limit the ability to achieve business goals. Turnover of permanent employees was 31.40% in FY 2025-26 (32.47% in FY 2024-25), a structurally high rate mitigated through attrition monitoring, case-by-case retention, induction and training, and compensation aligned to travel industry standards.
- Geopolitical disruption to aviation and international travel corridors — Management describes conflicts across Eastern Europe and the Middle East disrupting international aviation through airspace restrictions, longer routes, temporary airspace closures, flight cancellations and rerouting, which raised airline operating costs, affected capacity on certain international routes and weighed on travel confidence. This directly hit consumer demand in the opening quarter and parts of the MICE and international corporate travel business in the fourth quarter.
- Single-activity and single-sector concentration — BRSR Section A reports that 100% of turnover comes from one main activity - travel agency and tour operators (support service to organizations) - with Hotel and Packaging at 60.75% and Air Ticketing at 30.87% of turnover. Earnings are therefore fully exposed to the Indian travel cycle, airline capacity and fare dynamics, with no diversifying business line.
- Climate change, GHG emissions and energy efficiency in operations — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table: as a tour and travel business, direct emissions from electricity consumption combine with substantial Scope 3 emissions arising from airlines and hotel operations carried out by suppliers, requiring a business-responsibility response. Mitigation includes encouraging online meetings instead of travel, promoting eco-friendly travel options and working with travel partners sharing the sustainability commitment.
- Customer grievance volume and service reliability — The BRSR transparency and disclosures table records 10,758 customer complaints filed during FY 2025-26 (14,475 in FY 2024-25) with none pending at year end. In a category where management itself says trust, reliability and responsiveness are decisive purchase factors, sustained complaint volume of this scale is a structural service-delivery exposure.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Yatra is an asset-light travel platform, so its expansion is footprint, platform build-out and acquisitions rather than plant capacity. During FY 2025-26 the Company completed migration of its platform to Google Cloud, which management says improved scalability, partner connectivity and the ability to serve a wider ecosystem of travel buyers and suppliers, and invested in backend supply connectivity to extend the reach of its hotel content and scale transaction volumes. Inorganically, the acquisition of Globe Travel Services brought a client base of approximately 360 corporate accounts and MICE expertise, positioning the Company among the largest MICE players in India. Group structure was simplified when six wholly-owned subsidiaries merged into Yatra Online Limited with effect from December 01, 2025 under an NCLT-approved composite scheme of amalgamation. Geographic expansion is being pursued through a memorandum of understanding signed on July 13, 2026 between Yatra Online Limited, its wholly owned subsidiary Yatra Middle East LLC, Kanoo Global Travel Holding Limited and Yusuf Bin Ahmed Kanoo (Holdings) Co. B.S.C. (Closed) for a strategic technology arrangement in the Middle East, under which Kanoo Travel is expected to deploy Yatra's integrated enterprise travel and expense management platform and a Kanoo Travel Global Operations Centre is to be established providing 24x7 multilingual operational support across the region. Supply-side footprint expanded through direct relationships with 81,000 hotel properties, 400 domestic and international airlines and coverage of 1,500+ cities and destinations, a network of over 55,000 travel agents, and API-led distribution to travel agents and B2B partners. On the systems side, remediation of identified internal-control weaknesses includes upgrading the primary accounting software from MS Navision to D365 F&O. The annual report bundle does not state a rupee capital-expenditure quantum for any of this.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Corporate travel in India remains significantly under-penetrated, with more than 75% of corporates still dependent on offline booking processes; managed corporate travel penetration is approximately 25%, and the shift from fragmented offline models to integrated digital platforms is expected to continue
- India's corporate travel market is projected to grow to over USD 20 billion by FY 2026-27, with the TMC and corporate OTA share rising from 20.4% to 23% of corporate GBV
- Enterprise wins momentum: 163 new corporate customers added in the year, representing annual billable value of approximately Rs 9,568 million, supported by customer retention of nearly 97%
- Air volumes growing ahead of the market alongside margin discipline - fourth quarter Air passenger volumes up 9.6% year-on-year against industry passenger growth of about 1.2%, with Air margins improving from approximately 2.7% in FY 2023-24 to nearly 4% in FY 2025-26
- Hotels and Packages as a mix and margin lever - segment TTV growth of about 25% during the year with Hotel margins improving from 8.6% to 9.25%, reflecting better business mix, stronger monetization and deeper supplier relationships
- Supply-side expansion: India's domestic aviation market carried 167.74 million passengers in FY 2025-26, with continued airport infrastructure expansion and broader seat growth supporting demand across metro and Tier-2 markets
- Hospitality backdrop: ICRA projects hospitality industry revenues to grow 7% to 9% in FY 2026-27, following growth of 9% to 12% in FY 2025-26, supporting Yatra's hotel supply and MICE capabilities
- Geopolitical disruption is the near-term drag - cross-border tensions and aviation disruptions affected consumer demand in the opening quarter and hit MICE and international corporate travel in the fourth quarter, with demand shifting toward domestic travel; management expects much of the deferred demand to return as conditions normalise
- Structural demand support from rising incomes, a widening middle class, urbanisation, growing digital adoption and continued formalization of corporate travel management
- Traveller preference shifting from price toward reliability, flexibility and assurance, which management links to the industry's turn to AI for disruption management and servicing
- API-led distribution seen as a strategically important growth avenue with potential to add scale while remaining margin-accretive
- 163 new corporate clients signed during FY 2025-26, the highest number of enterprise wins in any single year in the Company's history, representing an annual billing potential of Rs 9,568 million
- Customer retention of nearly 97%, with 71% of the top 100 corporate customers retained for more than five years

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Yatra Online Limited is India's leading corporate travel services provider with over 1,300 corporate customers and one of India's leading online travel companies, operating the Yatra.com platform.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Yatra runs a multi-channel travel platform spanning direct-to-consumer, corporate travel and B2B distribution, serving leisure travellers, SMEs, large enterprises and travel agents through its website, mobile applications and partner network. Its portfolio covers domestic and international air travel, hotel accommodation and homestays, holiday packages, rail and bus bookings, cabs, cruises, MICE and ancillary travel services, with real-time access to over 80,000 hotels in India and more than 2 million accommodation options globally. Supported by a scalable technology platform, long-standing supplier relationships and a diversified distribution network, the company describes itself as having evolved beyond an online travel agency into an integrated travel management platform.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Corporate travel in India remains significantly under-penetrated, with more than 75% of corporates still dependent on offline booking processes; managed corporate travel penetration is approximately 25%, and the shift from fragmented offline models to integrated digital platforms is expected to continue
- India's corporate travel market is projected to grow to over USD 20 billion by FY 2026-27, with the TMC and corporate OTA share rising from 20.4% to 23% of corporate GBV
- Enterprise wins momentum: 163 new corporate customers added in the year, representing annual billable value of approximately Rs 9,568 million, supported by customer retention of nearly 97%
- Air volumes growing ahead of the market alongside margin discipline - fourth quarter Air passenger volumes up 9.6% year-on-year against industry passenger growth of about 1.2%, with Air margins improving from approximately 2.7% in FY 2023-24 to nearly 4% in FY 2025-26
- Hotels and Packages as a mix and margin lever - segment TTV growth of about 25% during the year with Hotel margins improving from 8.6% to 9.25%, reflecting better business mix, stronger monetization and deeper supplier relationships
- Supply-side expansion: India's domestic aviation market carried 167.74 million passengers in FY 2025-26, with continued airport infrastructure expansion and broader seat growth supporting demand across metro and Tier-2 markets
- Hospitality backdrop: ICRA projects hospitality industry revenues to grow 7% to 9% in FY 2026-27, following growth of 9% to 12% in FY 2025-26, supporting Yatra's hotel supply and MICE capabilities
- Geopolitical disruption is the near-term drag - cross-border tensions and aviation disruptions affected consumer demand in the opening quarter and hit MICE and international corporate travel in the fourth quarter, with demand shifting toward domestic travel; management expects much of the deferred demand to return as conditions normalise
- Structural demand support from rising incomes, a widening middle class, urbanisation, growing digital adoption and continued formalization of corporate travel management
- Traveller preference shifting from price toward reliability, flexibility and assurance, which management links to the industry's turn to AI for disruption management and servicing
- API-led distribution seen as a strategically important growth avenue with potential to add scale while remaining margin-accretive
- 163 new corporate clients signed during FY 2025-26, the highest number of enterprise wins in any single year in the Company's history, representing an annual billing potential of Rs 9,568 million
- Customer retention of nearly 97%, with 71% of the top 100 corporate customers retained for more than five years

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Air margin improved structurally from 2.7% (FY24) to 4% (FY26); Hotel margin 7.7% to 9.25%. Cost pressure: People cost up due to salary inflation and share-based payments in Q4; Discounting ratio optimized to ~48% of gross take (from 61% historically) driven by B2E mix.

capital_allocation.body: Net cash position INR 2,230mn; Strong operating cash flow INR 761mn (FY26) vs INR 73mn (FY25); Holding company (THCL) sold 1.8% stake to fund legal restructuring (NCLT merger of subsidiaries), no further dilution expected.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Yatra is an asset-light travel platform, so its expansion is footprint, platform build-out and acquisitions rather than plant capacity. During FY 2025-26 the Company completed migration of its platform to Google Cloud, which management says improved scalability, partner connectivity and the ability to serve a wider ecosystem of travel buyers and suppliers, and invested in backend supply connectivity to extend the reach of its hotel content and scale transaction volumes. Inorganically, the acquisition of Globe Travel Services brought a client base of approximately 360 corporate accounts and MICE expertise, positioning the Company among the largest MICE players in India. Group structure was simplified when six wholly-owned subsidiaries merged into Yatra Online Limited with effect from December 01, 2025 under an NCLT-approved composite scheme of amalgamation. Geographic expansion is being pursued through a memorandum of understanding signed on July 13, 2026 between Yatra Online Limited, its wholly owned subsidiary Yatra Middle East LLC, Kanoo Global Travel Holding Limited and Yusuf Bin Ahmed Kanoo (Holdings) Co. B.S.C. (Closed) for a strategic technology arrangement in the Middle East, under which Kanoo Travel is expected to deploy Yatra's integrated enterprise travel and expense management platform and a Kanoo Travel Global Operations Centre is to be established providing 24x7 multilingual operational support across the region. Supply-side footprint expanded through direct relationships with 81,000 hotel properties, 400 domestic and international airlines and coverage of 1,500+ cities and destinations, a network of over 55,000 travel agents, and API-led distribution to travel agents and B2B partners. On the systems side, remediation of identified internal-control weaknesses includes upgrading the primary accounting software from MS Navision to D365 F&O. The annual report bundle does not state a rupee capital-expenditure quantum for any of this.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established brand and decades-long presence in Indian travel, with roughly 80% of traffic arriving direct or organic rather than through paid acquisition
- Leadership in corporate travel with over 1,300 large and medium corporate clients and approximately 60,000 SME clients; described as India's leading B2B corporate platform by total spend and number of customers
- High customer stickiness: approximately 97% customer retention, with 71% of the top 100 corporate customers retained for more than five years
- Comprehensive end-to-end offering bringing flights, hotels, trains, buses, holiday packages, activities, cruises and corporate travel onto one platform
- Omni-channel distribution through a network of over 55,000 travel agents, extending reach into Tier-II and Tier-III cities
- Deep supply relationships: direct relationships with 81,000 hotel properties, 400 domestic and international airlines, and coverage of 1,500+ cities and destinations
- Single real-time integrated system across corporate and consumer travel, giving a centralised data base that the company argues most fragmented competitors lack and that is a prerequisite for AI/agentic deployment
- Asset-light business model that keeps fixed overheads lean, coupled with digital automation across key processes
- Broad partnership ecosystem spanning airlines, hotel groups, payment providers and tourism authorities
- Consumer scale: 16.2 million registered customers, 22 million+ mobile app downloads and 88 million total consumer visits

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
